project_metadata.job_description:
Wordpress site hosted with WP Engine has slow page load. Seeking developer to diagnose and fix the front-end performance issue.

Scope
- Diagnose root cause of slow page load
- Fix identified issues (assets, scripts, plugins, page builder elements — whatever the diagnosis shows)
- Verify improvement with before/after performance data
- Brief written summary of cause and fix

Requirements
- Proven experience fixing WordPress site speed issues (not just plugin installation)
- Comfortable with WP Engine hosting environment
- Able to read and act on tools like WebPageTest, GTmetrix, Lighthouse

The problem went beyond the fake admin users we found last night. I also discovered a hidden admin account buried in the database, with around 470 casino spam pages published through it. Code planted in one of your plugins was hiding all of this and interfering with the site's caching, which explains why pages were taking 15+ seconds to load for visitors.

The site has now been fully cleaned. It took About 7 hours in total today:
- Deleted the hidden admin account and all ~470 spam pages
- Replaced the altered plugin with a fresh official copy
- Reinstalled WordPress itself
- Coordinated with WP Engine to reset the site's credentials and keys, and requested a full platform-level malware scan as independent confirmation
- Configured Wordfence as a security scanner so it will alert us if anything suspicious occurs again

The outcome is that pages now load in under 2 seconds rather than 16, and I'll continue watching the site for the next couple of days to ensure it remains clean.

I need you to handle a few items:
1. The security reset signed everyone out of WordPress. When you sign back in, create a new password and have all other admins do the same
2. Update your WP Engine password as well, just as a precaution
3. Give me access to your Google Search Console so I can remove the spam pages from Google before they damage your rankings. Go to Settings > Users and permissions > Add user > Full access and use this email: [EMAIL_004]
4. Submit a quick test through the contact form and verify that the email arrives, confirming that your leads are still coming through after the changes

The following items remain on my list:
- Clean up Search Console once I have access
- Update the outdated plugins on your site (probably how the attackers originally gained access)
- Pass along WP Engine's scan results when they are available

I'm happy to answer any questions, and if you want one for your records, I can also provide a proper written report.
